uplink.description: full boat frame: BME280 air T/P/RH + dewpoint, 12.6V battery + batt temp, GNSS fix, two analog levels, bilge alarm + relay on
uplink._note: Synthetic in-bounds frame; expected.data produced by running reference/upstream-codec.js on this input and normalizing to the vocabulary (renamed keys, dropped upstream-hardcoded device/altitude/hdop and the redundant position object). Upstream level1 1.25 / level2 0 become the channels[] entries level0 / level1 with identical /100 scaling. air.pressure kept within the 900-1100 hPa vocabulary bound.

uplink.description: levels differ: both analog inputs non-zero and distinct (level0 3.75, level1 8.4), bilge clear, relay off
uplink._note: Synthetic multi-position frame: the first frame above with bytes[22..25] set to two distinct non-zero levels (375 and 840 little-endian, /100 -> 3.75 and 8.4) and byte 26 cleared. Cross-checked against reference/upstream-codec.js (level1 3.75, level2 8.4, alarm1 0, relay 0). Pins entry order to the wire order (bytes[22..23] -> level0, bytes[24..25] -> level1) and shows the two positions carrying different readings, which the old flat level1/level2 extras could not distinguish from a renumbering mistake.

uplink.description: low-battery boat frame: 9.85V triggers undervoltage warning, no bilge alarm, relay off
uplink._note: Synthetic in-bounds frame; expected.data produced by running reference/upstream-codec.js on this input and normalizing to the vocabulary. level0 reads 0 — a legitimate empty-tank value, not a disconnected-input sentinel (the frame defines none), so the entry is still emitted. Battery 9.85V is below the upstream 10V threshold; the codec emits a `warnings` array (declared here per the conformance contract: data vectors that emit warnings must declare them).
Synthetic error case: the fixed frame is 27 bytes; anything shorter cannot be decoded, so no `channels` key is emitted.
